title: White House Council of Economic Advisers reports growth in manufacturing sector
excerpt: The Council of Economic Advisers released an evaluation of the manufacturing sector on October 10, 2026.
bodyHtml:
The White House Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) released an evaluation of the United States manufacturing sector on October 10, 2026. The report states that the sector is experiencing growth under the policies of the Trump Administration.

According to the CEA, the United States is now the world's largest energy exporter. The report also notes that factory construction is increasing as a result of tariff policies, which incentivized companies to manufacture products within the United States.

The CEA analysis states that the manufacturing resurgence has positive impacts on the labor sector, including increased wages and company expansions that stimulate local economies. The report further claims that the United States is currently pioneering the technology frontier and reshoring production.

The report identifies several critical industries for national security that are positioned at the forefront of this manufacturing activity. These industries include aerospace, aircraft equipment, natural gas and petroleum production, and metals, with a new renaissance in American steel production reinforcing domestic industrial capacity.
